message: Reviewed from dated primary evidence using the Codex subscription.

data.headline: The UK raised rates. US yields had already moved.
data.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% this morning. The latest US observations tell a different, earlier story: Treasury yields rose on November 3, and secured overnight funding eased on November 4. The sequence matters when interpreting the two markets.

bull.text: US overnight secured funding eased: SOFR fell from 3.97% on November 3 to 3.94% on November 4. That is a modest reduction in the observed overnight rate.

bear.text: The UK vote was 8–1 for a quarter-point rise from 3.75% to 4%; the dissenter wanted a half-point rise to 4.25%. Members disagreed on how much to tighten, not on whether to tighten.

watch.text: On November 3 the US two-year yielded 4.61%, the ten-year 4.95% and the thirty-year 5.32%. A later US observation is needed to examine any move after the November 5 UK announcement.

limitations: The UK meeting ended November 4. The Bank released the minutes at 7 a.m. ET on November 5. No priced expectation or cross-market price reaction is measured.
The available evidence does not support a calibrated forecast or a directional trading call.
